description: Recorded fixture session for Cafe 210 (State College) — used by /api/mock-session/{id} and app.mock_debate.run_debate. Shapes mirror docs/api-contract.md v1.

evidence.claim: Weekend footfall peaks after 10 PM and regulars complain about the 11 PM close.
evidence.quote: "Wish they stayed open later on football Saturdays — the whole line was turned away at 11."

evidence.claim: Late-night food options on College Ave thin out after midnight on game days.
evidence.quote: Only three kitchens on the block keep the lights on past midnight during home games.

evidence.claim: Extended-close nights run roughly $180 of extra staff and utilities per night.
evidence.quote: Last extra-late Saturday cost about $180 in staff + utilities against $610 in late sales.

personas.name: Maya the junior
personas.profile: Junior who walks down from campus after every home game; her group always eats around midnight and gets shut out by the current close.

personas.name: Devon the freshman
personas.profile: Freshman with a meal plan he calls a suggestion; hungry at 1 AM on game days and follows the crowd to whoever is open.

personas.name: Frank the morning regular
personas.profile: Retiree who arrives at 6:30 AM sharp; afraid a 2 AM close means tired staff and slower mornings on Sundays.

personas.name: Rosa the afternoon regular
personas.profile: Works across the street, comes in most afternoons; neutral on closing hours but wary of price creep to cover late-night costs.

personas.name: Pete the visiting dad
personas.profile: In town twice a season for tailgates; with two teenagers he would spend on a late dessert stop if somewhere clean is open.

personas.name: Cleo the barista
personas.profile: Senior barista; open to closing late but only if there is a real cut of the late-night tips and a rideshare stipend.

snapshot.question: Should we stay open until 2 AM on football Saturdays?

verdict.recommendation: Stay open until 2 AM on the six home football Saturdays only, run by a small volunteer-style late crew with the game_day_special promo. The opposition is real — morning regulars may feel the cost — but the late-night demand gap (e1, e2) plus the strong late-sales vs. cost math (e3) makes the trade worth it, and returning to 11 PM closes in off-weeks protects the regulars.
objections: Morning regulars (Frank) fear a tired staff and slower Sunday mornings if the late crew overruns.
One strong late Saturday does not prove the next five will repeat at the same margin.
The students driving the late demand are the lowest-paycheck-per-visit crowd; the mix may skew late without covering fixed costs.

segment_impact.impact: +30% visits on home-game Saturdays after 1 AM
-10% morning visits from regulars annoyed by crowded Sundays
+15% dessert-and-drinks spend if a clean late option stays open

data.reason: My whole group walks out of Beaver Stadium starving at 12:30 and Cafe 210 is already dark. Two more hours is a crowd every time.
Anything open past midnight on game days owns the walk home. I'd bring six friends with zero loyalty to anyone else.
I'm there at 6:30 sharp; a 2 AM close means slow, grumpy staff on Sunday mornings.
Fine with late hours as long as my afternoon latte doesn't get pricier to pay for it.
With two teenagers we're hunting dessert at 12:45 and everywhere clean is shut.
I'd stay late only for a real cut of tips plus a rideshare stipend home.

top_arguments: Extra payroll and utilities eat thin margins on a single night's data
Worn-down staff show up slower on Sunday mornings, hurting the most loyal regulars
Three late kitchens on the block is zero competition for thousands of post-game walkers
Game-day demand is predictable: six Saturdays, packed at 12:30, ready to spend

data.reason: Skeptics are right that one night isn't proof — that's why it should be the six home games plus a buffer. I'd spend every one.
Hearing the cost math changed me — try midnight first and see if the line is real. I'll still show up at 12:30.
The skeptic case holds — margins are thin and Sunday is my whole routine. Don't risk my mornings.
Someone has to say it: a student deal plus late hours reads like a price hike for the rest of us.
Limit it to home games and we visiting families still get our late stop. Skeptic math works if you schedule the risk.
Without a committed tips-plus-stipend structure I'd vote no — staff burnout is the hidden cost no one is pricing.

top_arguments: Prove it at midnight first: run the 12:30 test night, not the full 2 AM commitment
No tips/stipend structure means the late shift quietly becomes everyone's problem
Schedule the risk: six home Saturdays only, evaluated after each one
Zero real competition after midnight on game days
